name: inventory-write-then-observe

graded_by.test: owed by the E3 U2 plan (a file change reaches the index with no request)
owed by the E3 U11 plan (rig-discovery: the real driver, fed a synthetic source)

description: The spine's C5 grade, quoted: "a file written by a discovery worker appears in the index without anyone asking it to". One write cycle of one source: the writer puts the target at a name a reader ignores (.lab-sw-07.yaml.tmp) in the same directory, then renames it over the target (x-layout rule 3), and writes only inside its own source directory (rule 4). The next read takes the renamed file — the temp name is not a target — and the entry appears in the index with no request from anyone. The rule is executable in tsbc (_inventory.inventory_read); this case is its record. `alerts` is the reader's report of what it refused; the core writes each as a log line (x-layout identity-and-refusals, missing-current). The file may be written by any writer (at E3 a rig); its mark, input and expected output stay.
